Clinical Treatment Summary
The patient presented following a low-speed rear-end collision in a parking lot, reporting neck pain, stiffness, and
headache consistent with whiplash-type cervical strain. The mechanism of injury described is plausible for a collision
of this nature. Imaging and physical examination findings clearly confirm soft tissue injury to the cervical region. The
patient's history includes a minor starin in the same area many years ago, which resolved completely without lasting
limitation. Over the course of fifteen visits, care included manual therapy, range-of-motion exercises, and a home
stretching program. Treatment followed a typical progression, with frequency tapering as symptoms improved and
range of motion returned toward baseline. At the most recent visit, the patient reported minimal residual discomfort
and full return to daily activities. Two similar billing entries recorded on the same day are currently under review for
accuracy. Discharge from active care is anticipated with a home exercise program and as-needed follow-up.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
